analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and metadata against the indexed model, including the detailed T-041 evidence. No concrete security regression is established in this scope. Autopilot/ProviderLoop+AutopilotInventory.swift:15 preserves adopted advertisements after control-lease expiry. ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift:22-49 constrains adoption/holds by saved consent, selection, residency, retirement, self-test and live hash availability; these are model-placement permissions, not evidence of App Attest authorization (T-052/T-053). Holds use monotonic expiry, and held-weight accounting saturates (:89-95). No prompt, key, billing or cache-scope data is added to the protocol telemetry; T-041 cache cryptography and TTL are not changed here.
ProviderLoop+TransitionWatchdog.swift:81-100 cancels owned operations, requests startup stopping, and answers stalled preloads without directly clearing allocation fences. TransitionWatchdog.swift:86-109 tracks continuous occurrences and reports each stall once. Protocol/Autopilot/ModelAutopilot.swift adds optional placement/busy/stall fields and hold_seconds; the decoding patch adds corresponding typed reads.
Integration must verify: command admission bounds hold_seconds to 0...86400 before Placement.swift:68-69 (unchecked multiplication otherwise can trap); placement recording occurs only after a successful owned operation; request/native admission retains current connection authorization independently of autopilotServesModel (T-053); consent/hash/build changes reconcile placements promptly (T-012/T-027); and finishPreloadTask at Watchdog.swift:96 leaves native-load ownership fenced and prevents stale completion from affecting a retry. Check idle/LRU consumers of holds against T-029 and cancellation cleanup against T-010. These callers are outside the supplied source, so their contracts are unresolved, not observed missing controls. Snapshot+Decoding.swift was supplied as metadata with a bounded change excerpt, not full surrounding source.
